thread:
alex: Quick follow-up on the dedicated-pool RFC — I'm proposing we add 'lease hints' to reduce churn during scale-downs. Idea: keep a tiny carryover of soft leases per-tenant for a short TTL instead of immediately evicting, so we avoid repeated prewarm/warmup costs.

maria: That sounds promising. How do you want to pick the TTL? static minutes or adaptive?

ton y: We should make it adaptive to request interarrival. Rough heuristic: lease_hint = min(30m, 2 * mean_interarrival_ms / (1 + cv)). Means noisy tenants keep short hints, steady ones get longer.

alex: Nice formula. Also want to pair with an eviction_budget so we don't starve other tenants during ramp-down. Proposal config snippet:
```
autoscale:
  scale_down:
    lease_hint_minutes: 15
    eviction_budget_pct: 5
```
jen: Main concern: what if a tenant simply stops paying or revokes credentials? We can't keep leaking GPU capacity because of hints. Need a hard eviction path after billing check fails.

alex: Agreed — two-tier approach: hinted leases (soft, short-lived) + soft-reservations (billing-guarded, requires tenant commit flag). If billing check fails soft-reservations are immediately reclaimed.

autoscaler-bot: scale-event: pool-78 scaled -1 GPU (03:21 UTC) — reason: idle threshold breached, eviction_budget used 3%.

sam: Also think about cost-smoothing on the spin-up side: don't spin up a whole GPU for tiny bursts. Use probabilistic burst tokens + short hop to hosted for spikes <5s. If spikes persist, promote to dedicated.

nisha: To operationalize we'll need metrics: per-tenant burst_rate, mean_busy_slot, prewarm_success_rate, and a 'preemption_cascade_window' counter so we can detect cascading evictions.

maria: Another edge: model warmup cost. If we evict by tenant but the model variant is the reason for warmup cost, we should cache at model-variant granularity instead of tenant. That reduces churn for multi-tenant same-model scenarios.

ton y: Interface boundary sketch: allocator returns two fields on lease grant: `lease_hint_ttl` and `eviction_priority` (0..100). Runtime uses `eviction_priority` combined with a global preemption budget to pick eviction candidates.

jen: Also need an automatic fallback path: if eviction will breach an endpoint SLO (e.g., gen endpoints), runtime should auto-fallback routed requests to hosted and mark the tenant with 'recommit needed' so CS can follow up. Avoids user-visible errors.

alex: Action items: (1) update RFC with `lease_hint_ttl` + `eviction_priority` and a sample config for `eviction_budget_pct` (2) add `prewarm_threshold_ms` knob so we prewarm only when expected benefit > cost (3) define metric names and dashboard wireframe. I'll open a PR after this thread.

sam: :thumbsup: I'll add a sim harness test that replays burst patterns and preemption sequences — can reuse sim-runner from eng-runtime/sim.

maria: I'll own the dashboards for the new metrics. @jen please take billing edge cases.

alex: Thanks all — I'll file the PR and link the updated RFC and a small unit test for the allocator interface.

jen: One more note — add a short timeout for telemetry propagation; otherwise eviction decisions will be based on stale metrics during rapid scale events.

alex: Good call. Adding `telemetry_freshness_ms` to the config list. Will post PR in ~1h.
